rows.figure: 1,455 fatalities from 50 accidents in 2025 (known fatalities, Baird Maritime Passenger Vessel Accident database)
rows.scope: Known deaths in fatal passenger-vessel accidents worldwide in calendar 2025, from the Baird Maritime Passenger Vessel Accident (BMPVA) database as reported in the publisher's annual editorial. Editorials say ferry fatalities, but the database covers passenger vessels broadly: tour boats were 34% of its 2025 accidents; cruise ships had 3 deaths. No definition of a ferry, no fatality threshold and no statement on missing persons is printed; IMO's project paper calls Baird's counts persons reported dead or missing. Leaves out unreported accidents (Myanmar, North Korea) and non-passenger craft.
rows.source: Baird Maritime, editorial 'Passenger vessel death toll falls 28 per cent in 2025; tour boats become an increasing problem', published 8 Jan 2026, reporting the publisher's own BMPVA database
rows.do_not_add_to: Known deaths only, from one trade publisher's media-based database; outside the WHO drowning figure by definition. Do not add to the WFSA rows (different threshold and period, overlapping events), to the Interferry or LRF figures, or to water-transport-other. Not a count of fishing, cargo, migrant or private small-craft deaths. Do not add Baird years together: each year is the source's own total.
rows.note: Most recent year available. The same editorial repeats 2024 as 2,033 from 55 accidents and 2023 as 1,308 from 39, unchanged. DR Congo 807 deaths from 6 accidents and Nigeria 292 from 7 in 2025, per the same editorial. The source revises earlier years in later editorials, so cite the latest editorial for any year.

rows.figure: 284 ferry accidents with 21,996 fatalities worldwide, 2000 to end of 2018 (cumulative; dead and missing listed together)
rows.scope: Cumulative 19-year total of dead and missing in fatal ferry accidents worldwide in the Worldwide Ferry Safety Association database, built from media reports since 2000 with almost no official investigative reports. The WFSA counting rule, printed in its 2016 Journal of Public Transportation paper, is accidents with two or more deaths of passengers and/or crew. No definition of a ferry is printed. Leaves out accidents not reported in the media; the article calls DR Congo data incomplete and says Lake Victoria fishermen deaths are not ferry accidents. Southern Hemisphere: 91 accidents, 7,029.
rows.source: Worldwide Ferry Safety Association, 'Disproportionate numbers: Tracking ferry safety in the Southern Hemisphere', Maritime Technology, July 2019, pp. 48-54, PDF hosted on ferrysafety.org (section 'By the numbers')
rows.do_not_add_to: Cumulative over 19 years: never divide into a per-year figure and never add to or compare with the Baird yearly rows, which use a different database, threshold and vessel scope and overlap in events. Outside the WHO drowning figure by definition. Do not add to ferry-wfsa-jpt-2016, whose period is nested inside this one.
rows.note: The most recent WFSA total found. WFSA's homepage (read 21 Oct 2026) says it maintains a database with 25 data points for each fatal accident since 2000, but no yearly table, annual statistics page or newer total is published on ferrysafety.org; the WFSA Annual Report 2023 PDF contains no statistics. The 2019 article says WFSA and the Baird database holder exchange datasets.

rows.figure: 232 ferry accidents, 21,574 lives lost, 2000 to 2014 (the paper prints an average of 1,541 deaths per year)
rows.scope: Cumulative 14-year tally of dead and missing in major ferry accidents worldwide from the Worldwide Ferry Safety Association database, peer-reviewed. Inclusion rule (Methods, p. 18): only accidents with deaths of two or more passengers and/or crewmembers. Table 1 labels the count 'Fatalities (dead and missing)'. Sources: news sources worldwide, incident investigation reports where available, and IMO GISIS. The paper calls the tally conservative and based on news reports, noting sparse media coverage, unrecorded overcrowding and unpublished investigations. No ferry definition; 43 countries.
rows.source: Journal of Public Transportation, vol. 19 no. 1, 2016, 'Trends, Causal Analysis, and Recommendations from 14 Years of Ferry Accidents' (WFSA database analysis; full text on USF Digital Commons; DOI prefix 10.5038, suffix 2375 0901.19.1.2 with a hyphen between the two four-digit groups)
rows.do_not_add_to: Cumulative; the 1,541 per year and 130 per incident are the source's own averages, not the lab's. Do not add to ferry-wfsa-cumulative-to-2018 (nested period) or to any Baird yearly row. Outside the WHO drowning figure by definition.
rows.note: This is the only published statement of the WFSA database's counting rule found. The paper has no year-by-year table (Table 1 covers causes; Figures 1 and 2 country shares). The abstract calls the 232 events 'major accidents' without a separate definition beyond the two-death threshold.

rows.figure: 750 recorded fatal accidents involving passenger vessels, 59,600 fatalities, 1966 to 2015; averaged more than 1,000 fatalities per year since the 1960s
rows.scope: Cumulative 50-year total of known fatalities in recorded fatal passenger-vessel accidents worldwide, as analysed in the Lloyd's Register Foundation Insight report on safety in the passenger ferry industry (2018). notes: Key finding: no primary body publishes a public year-by-year table of ferry deaths. The only yearly series found is the Baird Maritime Passenger Vessel Accident (BMPVA) database, whose owner prints each year's total in an annual editorial on bairdmaritime.com: 2021 1,378 (25 accidents; first printed 1,380/26), 2022 699 (41), 2023 1,308 (39), 2024 2,033 (55), 2025 1,455 (50); 2020 264 (20; first printed 238/19). IMO's own domestic ferry safety project paper and the Lloyd's Register Foundation 2018 Insight report both rely on this database, and the WFSA's 2019 article says WFSA and the Baird database holder exchange datasets, so it is the de facto reference compilation. Status is 'partial' because the acceptance check asks for the source's own definition of a ferry and of a death, and Baird prints neither: it reports 'known' fatalities, calls them ferry fatalities in headlines but counts passenger vessels broadly (tour boats 34% of 2025 accidents; cruise ships 3 deaths in 2025), never states whether missing persons are counted (IMO's paper describes the counts as persons 'reported dead or missing'), and is inconsistent on its own start date (1966 in Feb 2022, 1983 in Feb 2024). Until 2017 the publisher added a 50% allowance for unknown fatalities to produce an estimate; the 2020 to 2025 figures are known deaths only, and the publisher says the real number is almost certainly significantly higher. Rows are graded C because the figures are a trade publisher's own media-based compilation printed in editorials, not official data or peer review, even though bairdmaritime.com is the producing organisation. The WFSA's own database rule (two or more deaths of passengers and/or crew; dead and missing together; news reports, investigation reports and GISIS) is printed in its 2016 Journal of Public Transportation paper (grade B row), and its latest public total is cumulative, 284 accidents and 21,996 fatalities for 2000 to 2018 (grade C row). Caution on the ferry-wfsa ledger row: its 'source' field currently names a person; rule 3 says no names, so a maintainer should trim it to the organisation and the person's title without my copying the name into a correction. The 2025 Baird editorial was opened at its amp URL; the canonical URL is presumably the same path without '/amp/story', untested. What a person with a browser should check: (1) read the bars of Figure 1 in the LRF report for yearly values; (2) open the WFSA xlsx for 2000 to 2015 yearly rows; (3) with an IMO GISIS login, pull lives lost on passenger/ro-ro passenger ships by year 2020 to 2025 from the Marine Casualties and Incidents module for an official, if incomplete, comparison; (4) check the Baird editorials of early 2019 and early 2020 for full-year 2018 and 2019 totals. No file in the repository was edited.
